newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian diamond trade Q1 strong but margins shrink.
newsitem.headline: Belgian diamond trade Q1 strong but margins shrink.

text.p: Belgium's diamond trade, the world's biggest, said on Wednesday that business in the first quarter of 1997 had been strong but dogged by dwindling profit margins and a shift by consumers to cheaper qualities of gems.
"The new year brought a strong start for the Antwerp diamond trade," the Diamond High Council (DHC) said in a statement.
But because profit margins shrunk, diamond merchants needed increased activity to maintain their level of income, it said.

Imports in the first quarter soared 60 percent to 71 million carats in weight and rose three percent to $3 billion in value, compared with the same 1996 period. Exports jumped 51 percent to 65.8 million carats and three percent to $3 billion in value.
Overall volume rose 56 percent in weight to 137 million carats and three percent in value to $6.29 billion.
"The higher rise of the trade in weight compared to the volume indicates that the diamond market worldwide moves towards cheaper qualities," the DHC said.
But retail sales of jewellery in the United States showed a positive trend and was again turning into a quality-gem market.
The DHC said the price rise for rough better-quality stones was affecting the price of polished diamonds.

It said that on the Antwerp market, the price of polished gems, mainly one-carat and to a lesser extent 0.50 carat stones, had started rising from the second half of 1996. The price of smaller diamonds had dropped.
The DHC said there were still a number of uncertainties which could have a major impact on the world diamond market.
One unsolved question was the development of negotiations between De Beers and Russia and whether Russia would adhere to a possible deal, it said.
De Beers, frustrated by Russian hesitation over a draft trade agreement submitted to the cabinet in October 1996, stopped buying gems from Moscow at the end of last year.
Other uncertainties included the situation in former Zaire, the future of Hong Kong after its return to Chinese rule and whether Japan could emerge from its economic problems.
